synopsis: OSHA rules are law rather than standards; compliance with standards does not establish compliance with law, or vice versa [f2145, f15010]. For machines with obstructed rear views, OSHA rules 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4) and 1926.602(a)(9)(ii) require a reverse alarm audible above surrounding noise or an observer, but specify neither a numeric range nor an automatic-braking mandate [f15505, f15508]. OSHA interpretation letters conditionally accept cameras that genuinely provide a clear rear view, removing the obstructed-view trigger, and radar or doppler warnings that are adequate and timely [f2229, f2230, f15506, f15507]. The glossary summarizes these as alternatives to reverse alarms, while Chapter 3 distinguishes the camera's removal of the trigger from radar's satisfaction of the warning requirement [f15072, f2229, f2230]. The research found no provision in OSHA or the other listed off-road regulatory and standards frameworks allowing simulation to replace a prescribed physical performance test, leaving virtual validation without an identified substitution route [f2103, f2475].

relations.note: Both report no identified provision allowing simulation to replace prescribed physical tests.
